scope: One finite minimum-cardinality interval product-cover index, all minimum witnesses, and saved product-period queries; no global g(n) claim.

mathematical_conventions.values: A nonempty set of distinct integers at least 2; duplicate input records are deduplicated.
mathematical_conventions.interval: I_x={x+1,...,x+M}, M=max A, integer x>=0; endpoints included.
mathematical_conventions.target: P=product(A) divides the product of distinct selected interval elements.
mathematical_conventions.optimum: Minimum selected cardinality, with the complete family of all minimum subsets.
mathematical_conventions.rank: Zero-based lexicographic order of increasing selected offset lists.
mathematical_conventions.exact_budget: Feasible iff minimum<=h<=M, by padding; other-size family counts are not supplied.
mathematical_conventions.source_wording: Erdos's 1992 paper says find g(n) integers; at-most is not asserted as a literal quotation or an authoritative resolution of the global definition.
mathematical_conventions.period: P is a valid offset period, not necessarily the least period.
